problem: Classical modular navigation generalizes but is error-prone due to multi-stage design and hand-crafted rules; learning-based visual navigation (ViNT, NoMaD) gets high success but generalizes poorly to out-of-distribution scenes, e.g. unseen random obstacles, and needs heavy training.
motivation: RGB-only local navigation in unknown environments needs collision-free paths in real time without maps or depth sensors. Diffusion models sample multimodal paths, so explicit classical costs can be injected at inference time (like classifier guidance) without retraining.
key_idea: Train a conditional diffusion model on path-RGB pairs, then at inference guide denoising with gradients of differentiable goal and collision costs (TSDF costmap from Depth Anything V2 monocular depth), plus a consistency-based path selection.
insight: Ablation shows that the same diffusion model without guidance performs about like NoMaD, whereas adding cost guidance lifts success sharply in obstacle and long-range tasks (e.g. indoor image-goal obstacle 52% -> 100%, collisions 0.43 -> 0.08). So the gain comes from inference-time explicit costs rather than from the learned prior. Guidance scale trades path diversity against goal precision.
method: Conditional diffusion planner: DDPM predicts waypoint paths conditioned on RGB observation sequence (and image goal) via encoders and a transformer; trained with noise-prediction MSE on RECON, SCAND, GoStanford and SACSoN; K=10 sampling steps.
Cost-guided sampling: classifier guidance is replaced by the gradient of an explicit cost, adding s_t*∇F(P;O) at each reverse step, with no retraining (plug-and-play).
Goal cost: Euclidean distance between the last waypoint and the point goal, F_g=||W0-G_p||; the scale trades diversity against precision.

Collision cost: Depth Anything V2 monocular depth -> local TSDF -> Gaussian-smoothed differentiable costmap; the cost sums the map values at each waypoint and at ±σR lateral offsets (half the robot width), with distance-increasing weights.
Total cost F=αF_g+βF_c; image-goal tasks use only the collision cost, point-goal tasks use both (weights 0.03 goal, 0.006 collision).

Path selection: choose among sampled candidates the one consistent with the previously chosen direction (proportion within an angle threshold), then apply weighted average filtering with the history for continuity.

setting.backbone: Conditional diffusion model with visual encoders + transformer (trained from scratch, NoMaD-style); frozen Depth Anything V2 for costs
setting.training_data: RECON, SCAND, GoStanford, SACSoN path-image datasets (same as NoMaD/ViNT baselines); trained ~39 h on one RTX TITAN, batch 256
setting.observation: monocular RGB sequence (+ image goal or point goal); depth estimated from RGB
setting.action_space: predicted waypoint paths (local planner, tracked by controller; 0.5 m/s, 0.4 rad/s in real world)
setting.simulator: Gazebo (Citysim outdoor), Stanford 2D-3D-S indoor; real world
setting.privileged: none (long-horizon subgoals come from a topological map for image goals / high-level policy)

numbers.extra: collision guidance + path selection; no fine-tuning on target scenes

Length is mean ± variance for successful trials. Ablation (w/o guidance) rows and baselines exist in Table I but are not listed here. Real-world results are qualitative only.
results: With guidance NaviDiffusor reaches 100% success in indoor basic and obstacle image-goal tasks and 74% in long-range (vs NoMaD 86/58/40%). Outdoors it gets 98/92/68% image-goal and 100/86/82% point-goal, with far fewer collisions and shorter paths than ViNT and NoMaD. Removing guidance drops it to NoMaD-like performance.
limitations: Requires hand-designed cost functions and hand-tuned parameters (weights, guidance scale)
Evaluated only in custom simulation scenes with 50 trials each and qualitative real-world demos; no standard benchmark
Depends on monocular depth estimation quality (Depth Anything V2) and on a high-level topological policy for long-range goals
